sources.title: 2026 Government greenhouse gas conversion factors: methodology paper

facts.source_fact: Material-use factors are for procured products and materials and distinguish primary from recycled material origin.
Material-use factors are not suitable for quantifying the benefit of collecting products or materials for recycling.
facts.expected_handling: Do not use as recycling-benefit metric.

facts.source_fact: Primary-material factors cover extraction, primary processing, manufacture and transport to the point of sale.
Primary-material factors do not cover impacts while the material is in use.
Secondary-material factors cover sorting, processing, manufacture and transport to the point of sale.
Secondary-material factors also exclude impacts while the material is in use.
The factors can support reporting of reduced procurement or procurement of products made from previously recycled material.
Material-use and waste-disposal sources are separated in the workbook to support separate Scope 3 reporting.
facts.expected_handling: Keep material and waste sources distinct.

facts.source_fact: There were no major methodological changes to material-use factors in 2026; changes reflect updated freight factors.
Material-use conversion factors are accounting factors, not parcel-level measurements of embodied emissions.
